blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Manasseh. Fifty-five years in Jerusalem, the longest reign in Judah.
REIGNEDi
55 years c. 697–643 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 14th of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✕ Did evil “And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, after the abominations of the heathen”
PROPHETS
"His servants the prophets" (unnamed) · "The seers" (unnamed)
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, after the abominations of the heathen”
2 Kings 21:2 (KJV) →
“and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Israel”
2 Kings 21:3 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
Kings: he "seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the LORD destroyed", and "shed innocent blood very much". 2 Kings 21:9 2 Kings 21:16
Kings later names his sins as the reason Judah was removed, "which the LORD would not pardon". 2 Kings 23:26 2 Kings 24:3–4
Chronicles adds his capture, his prayer, his return and his reform: "Then Manasseh knew that the LORD he was God." 2 Chronicles 33:11–16
CHRONICLES GIVES IT AS
“But did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, like unto the abominations of the heathen”
2 Chronicles 33:2 (KJV) →
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
Baal altars, a grove, the host of heaven, enchantments and wizards. 2 Kings 21:3–6
After his return the people still sacrificed on the high places, "yet unto the LORD their God only" (Chronicles). 2 Chronicles 33:17
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
Hi "His servants the prophets" (unnamed) “Behold, I am bringing such evil upon Jerusalem and Judah, that whosoever heareth of it, both his ears shall tingle.”
Th "The seers" (unnamed) Chronicles refers to "the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the LORD God of Israel".

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
55 years (2 Kgs 21:1). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Shared rule with Hezekiah, 697–687 BC
Printed form: 687/686–643/642; co-regency from 697 (PDF p. 34).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
Shared rule with Hezekiah, 697–687 BC
Printed form: 687/686–643/642; co-regency from 697/696 (p. 246 (Table 2)).
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 687–642 (p. 22).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Printed form: 698–643 (p. 74 (scan leaf n42)). The 1658 margin misprints the year as 694 [sic]; its own year-of-the-world column gives 698.
Credible
Ellicott's commentary (C. J. Ball, about 1883); W. E. Barnes (1899)
Assyrian records show Manasseh as an Assyrian vassal, and a captive king being restored has a parallel in Necho I of Egypt, put in fetters and sent back. 2 Chronicles 33:11–13 [43][153]
The captivity possible, the repentance late
W. E. Barnes (1899)
Some doubt the repentance because Kings condemns Manasseh without reserve; Barnes notes the Chronicler gives no date, so the restoration may belong to his last years. 2 Kings 21:1–18 [160]
Hard to fit with the contemporary sources
F. K. Sanders (Jewish Encyclopedia, 1904); E. G. Hirsch and W. H. Bennett (Jewish Encyclopedia, 1903)
Silence elsewhere does not make the story imaginary, but it rests on the unsupported testimony of a late source; some regard it as wholly unhistorical. 2 Chronicles 33:11–19 [72][67]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 7
2 Kings 20 2 Kings 21 2 Kings 23 2 Kings 24 2 Chronicles 32 2 Chronicles 33 Jeremiah 15
PASSAGES · 7
2 Kings 20:21 2 Kings 21:1–18 2 Kings 23:26 2 Kings 24:3–4 2 Chronicles 32:33 2 Chronicles 33:1–20 Jeremiah 15:4
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name the king of Assyria whose captains took Manasseh, or date the capture within his reign.
Scripture does not say how Isaiah died. A later tradition that he was killed under Manasseh is not in the Bible.
Kings does not mention a repentance.
